reason: DT-GSK was too slow on CEC2013LSGO (D=1000/905, MaxFES=3e6 ~ 50 min/run). Profiling isolated the cost: the objective is ~2% of wall time (numba-JIT) and the ISM interaction-graph block extraction is ~80%. Within it, interaction_graph._split_component re-derived the within-set row-sums Wn[rem][:,rem].sum(axis=1) by materialising a fresh |rem|x|rem| submatrix on every greedy iteration (~240 MB of copies per call at D=1000). This CR replaces that with a zero-allocation numba kernel (ig_component_rowsum_fast in _numba_accel.py) that reads Wn through the index in place. ~2.3-3x faster on CEC2013LSGO; the full ISM subsystem stays ACTIVE (not disabled). Performance only.
evidence: Bit-identity certified. The reference Wn[idx][:,idx].sum(axis=1) is a fancy-indexed reduction which NumPy evaluates with its NAIVE strided loop (left-to-right in idx order), not the pairwise SIMD path used for plain-contiguous arrays -- shown by a crafted [1e16,1,1,...] row: fancy returns 1e16 (naive), plain returns 1.0000000000001008e16 (pairwise). The kernel accumulates in the same idx order, so it reproduces the reference to the last bit. Unit parity: 848/848 real (captured D=1000) + adversarial random cases, max abs diff 0.0. End-to-end best_fitness bit-identical: cec2017 F3 D50 90113.3156549878, F5 D50 745.7618813989388, F3 D100 316049.9747246865, cec2013lsgo F1 D1000 52449801968.83455. reason: Threefry scalar-draw overhead dominated the GSK family on CEC2013LSGO. Post-CR-0009 profiling at a representative budget (150k/300k differencing, F1 D1000, production threefry) attributed 26-39% of wall time to the RNG for five classics and 68.9% for atmals-gsk, whose local search draws scalars per dimension per elite (atmals_gsk.py:98,100). Root cause was NOT the fill kernel (already unrolled 4.19x by 61dc84bd8) and NOT a missing batch (_draw already buffers 4 doubles/call): it was per-call Python overhead -- np.empty(1) allocation plus 'self._buffer = self._buffer[take:]', which constructs a fresh ndarray view object on EVERY draw. Naive batching was rejected as non-bit-identical: the draw count is data-dependent (line 100 draws only when line 98's test passes), so pre-drawing shifts the stream.

reason: Acceleration Wave 2.1: realized the author-authorized _rng_3buf fast path in DT-GSK as ONE fused flat core-stream draw. Production previously took three separate (N,D) draws per generation from rngs.core (both the linkage-off and scalar-rows branches of _dt_core.py); the pre-allocated (3*NP_init,D) buffer and its Generator.random(out=...) path were DEAD CODE -- unreachable because ReferenceRNG.uses_reference_matrix_order is a class attribute True for every generator, and the out= path would in fact have filled C-order, NOT reproducing the three column-major draws (the old B04 comment claiming 'no determinism break' was wrong; the guard protecting against it was load-bearing). The fused form draws rng_core.random(3*n) once and views segment k as reshape(D,N).T.
evidence: Bit-identical BY CONSTRUCTION: a shaped (N,D) draw is _draw(N*D) + reshape(D,N).swapaxes, so element [i,j] is the stream double at start+j*N+i; _draw is concatenation-consistent (Threefry doubles are a pure function of block index, the reservoir carries partial-block tails, so _draw(a)+_draw(b) consumes exactly the positions of _draw(a+b)); therefore segment k of the fused draw occupies exactly draw k's absolute stream positions, the identical reshape maps each element to the same 8 bytes, and the generator end state (counter + unconsumed tail) is unchanged. The .T views preserve the F-order layout downstream numba mask kernels always received.
